text: Scene 12  A visit from an old friend.
speaker: C5

text: On the eve of his thirty-eighth birthday Dorian arrived home from Lord Henry’s to find an old friend leaving the house.
speaker: C6

text: Dorian! I have been waiting for you since nine o'clock. I sent your poor servant to bed as I left. I am off to Paris by the midnight train and I wanted to see you before I go. I shan’t be back for six months and I want to talk with you.
speaker: BASIL

text: But won't you miss your train?
speaker: Dorian

text: All I have with me is in this bag, and I can easily get to Victoria in time. I must speak to you.
speaker: BASIL

text: You had better come in.
speaker: Dorian

text: Reluctantly Dorian ushered him in.
speaker: C6

text: They stood as strangers where once they stood as friends
speaker: C8

text: Basil lined with the weight of years
speaker: C5

text: and Dorian… unlined, unblemished, unchanged
speaker: C6

text: You should know that the most dreadful things are being said against you. But how can I believe these rumours now that I see you. Sin is a thing that writes itself across a man’s face. But you, with your pure, bright, innocent face - it is hard to believe anything against you.
speaker: BASIL

text: Don’t talk of rumours. I love scandals about other people, but scandals about myself don't interest me - even when they are true.
speaker: Dorian

text: You don't want people to talk of you as something vile and degraded. Position and wealth are not everything.
speaker: BASIL

text: What is your point Basil?
speaker: Dorian

text: I hear the most hideous things that people are whispering about you - vile rumours of the utmost degradation. You have been seen going into the most depraved areas of London. What need have you of opium dens? You have everything you need. Why would you seek oblivion in this way?
speaker: BASIL

text: As Harry says. To cure the soul by means of the senses and the senses by means of the soul.
speaker: Dorian

text: Harry! I wish you had never met him and yet even he is not spoken of the way you are.
speaker: BASIL

text: Enough! You are talking about things of which you know nothing.
speaker: Dorian

text: One has a right to judge a man by the effect he has on his friends. Yours seem to lose all sense of honour, of goodness, of purity. You have filled them with a madness for pleasure. They have been drawn down into the depths. You led them there. And there is worse behind. Drawing Harry’s sister there and making her name a by-word.
speaker: BASIL

text: Take care. You go too far.
speaker: Dorian

text: I must speak, and you must listen. They say that you corrupt every one with whom you become intimate, and that you only have to enter a house for shame to follow after. I don't know whether it is so or not. Before I could answer that, I should have to see your soul.
speaker: BASIL

text: To see my soul!
speaker: Dorian

text: Yes, but only God can do that.
speaker: BASIL

text: Well you shall see it yourself, tonight! Why shouldn't you look at it? It is your own handiwork. I will show you my soul Basil.
speaker: Dorian

text: This is blasphemy! You must not say things like that.
speaker: BASIL

text: I keep a diary of my life from day to day, and it never leaves the room in which it is written. I shall show it to you if you come with me.
speaker: Dorian

text: If you wish it. I see I have already missed my train. But I can go tomorrow. All I want is a plain answer.
speaker: BASIL

text: That shall be given to you upstairs. You will not have to read long.
speaker: Dorian

text: You insist on knowing, Basil?
speaker: Dorian

text: Yes.
speaker: BASIL

text: I am delighted. You are the one man in the world who is entitled to know everything about me.
speaker: Dorian

text: Taking up the lamp, he opened the door and went in.
speaker: C5

text: A cold current of air passed them.
speaker: C8

text: A dark animal scent filled Basil’s nostrils.
speaker: C5

text: So you think that it is only God who sees the soul, Draw that curtain back, and you will see mine.
speaker: Dorian

text: You are mad, or playing a part.
speaker: BASIL

text: You won't? Then I must do it myself. (Pulls back curtain)
speaker: Dorian

text: In the dim light the hideous face on the canvas seemed to grin at Basil. It filled him with disgust and loathing.
speaker: C6

text: It was Dorian Gray's own face. The horror had not entirely spoiled that marvellous beauty.
speaker: C5

text: There was still some ebony in the thinning hair and some scarlet on the sensual mouth.
speaker: C8

text: The sunken eyes had kept some of their amber glow blue.
speaker: C5

text: Basil groaned. It was some foul parody. He had never painted that.
speaker: C6

text: But it was his own picture. He knew it, and he felt as if his blood had changed from fire to ice.
speaker: C8

text: What does this mean?
speaker: BASIL

text: Years ago, when I was a boy, you finished a portrait of me that revealed to me the wonder of beauty. Then you introduced me to a friend, who explained to me the wonder of youth. In a mad moment I made a wish, perhaps you would call it a prayer....
speaker: Dorian

text: No! the thing is impossible. The room is damp. Mildew has got into the canvas.
speaker: BASIL

text: Ah, what is impossible?
speaker: Dorian

text: You told me you had destroyed it.
speaker: BASIL

text: I was wrong. It has destroyed me.
speaker: Dorian

text: I don't believe it is my picture.
speaker: BASIL

text: It is the face of my soul.
speaker: Dorian

text: Basil held the light up to the canvas. The surface was undisturbed.
speaker: C6

text: It was from within that the foulness and horror had come.
speaker: C5

text: The leprosies of sin were slowly eating the thing away.
speaker: C8

text: Christ! what a thing I have worshipped! It has the eyes of a devil. My God! If this is what you have done with your life you are more depraved than they know. What an awful lesson.
speaker: BASIL

text: (Dorian is sobbing)
speaker: Stage

text: Pray, Dorian, pray. The prayer of your pride has been answered, the prayer of your repentance will save you. I worshipped you too much - I am punished for it. Let’s pray together.
speaker: BASIL

text: It is too late, Basil
speaker: Dorian

text: Don't say that. My God! Don't you see that accursed thing leering at us?
speaker: BASIL

text: Dorian turned to the picture.
speaker: C5

text: And as though it had been suggested to him by the image on the canvas.
speaker: C6

text: Whispered into his ear by those grinning lips.
speaker: C8

text: Hate, hate, hate (keep going)
speaker: Ensemble

text: A wild rush of hatred swept over him.
speaker: C5

text: The knife
speaker: C

text: The knife, the knife (keep going)
speaker: Ensemble

text: His eye fell on the knife.
speaker: C6

text: He moved slowly towards it.
speaker: C5

text: Seizing the knife he rushed at Basil
speaker: C8

text: stabbing again and again and again.
speaker: All C

text: He left the thing in the playroom
speaker: C5

text: locked the door, and crept quietly downstairs.
speaker: C6

text: The woodwork creaked
speaker: C8

text: and seemed to cry out as if in pain.
speaker: C5

text: It was merely the sound of his own footsteps
speaker: C6

text: yet he could not disperse the feeling
speaker: C8

text: that something walked alongside him.
speaker: All 4

text: He put on his coat and hat and went out into the hall to the heavy oak door. Then he slipped out, shutting the door gently behind him, turned and rang the bell.
speaker: Dorian

text: His valet appeared.
speaker: FRANCIS

text: I am sorry to wake you up, Francis but I have forgotten my latch-key. What time is it?
speaker: Dorian

text: Ten minutes past two, sir.
speaker: FRANCIS

text: Ten minutes past two? How horribly late! Did anyone call this evening?
speaker: Dorian

text: Mr. Hallward, sir. He stayed here til eleven, and then he went away to catch his train. He said he would write to you from Paris.
speaker: FRANCIS

text: I am sorry to miss him. That will do, Francis. Don't forget to call me at nine to-morrow. I need you to take an urgent message to Alan Campbell in Mayfair. He is the very man I need.
speaker: Dorian

text: The next morning letter was delivered.
speaker: FRANCIS

text: The recipient recoiled in horror when he saw who had sent it.
speaker: ALAN

text: But he answered the summons.
speaker: FRANCIS

text: Alan! This is kind of you. Thank you for coming. (he holds out his hand)
speaker: Dorian

text: (ignoring Dorian’s hand) I had intended never to enter your house again, Gray. But you said it was a matter of life and death.
speaker: ALAN

text: A matter of death anyway. Alan, in a locked room at the top of this house, a dead man is seated at a table. He has been dead ten hours now.
speaker: Dorian

text: I don't want to know anything further. Keep your sordid secrets to yourself.
speaker: ALAN

text: You are the one man who is able to save me. You know about chemistry and have carried out experiments. You must destroy the thing upstairs - change it into a handful of ashes.
speaker: Dorian

text: You are mad to imagine that I would raise a finger to help you. I will have nothing to do with this matter. What is it to me what devil's work you are up to?
speaker: ALAN

text: Do you refuse to do this for me?
speaker: Dorian

text: I will have nothing to do with it. I don't care what shame comes on you. I should to be sorry to see you disgraced - publicly Disgraced. How dare you ask me, of all men, to mix myself up in this horror?
speaker: ALAN

text: We were friends once, Alan.
speaker: Dorian

text: Don’t speak about those days - they are dead. I absolutely refuse to do anything in the matter.
speaker: ALAN

text: (Dorian takes a piece of paper, and writes something on it and gives it to ALAN)
speaker: Stage

text: You see the address? If you don't help me, I must send it. You know what the result will be.
speaker: Dorian

text: Campbell opened the note,
speaker: C2

text: His face became ghastly pale.
speaker: C5

text: A horrible sense of sickness came over him.
speaker: C4

text: His heart was beating himself to death in some ghastly hollow.
speaker: C2

text: I cannot do it.
speaker: ALAN

text: You have no choice.
speaker: Dorian

text: I shall have to go home and get some equipment.
speaker: ALAN

text: No, you must not leave this house. Write out what you want and my servant will fetch it.
speaker: Dorian

text: You are infamous! You have gone from corruption to corruption. I have to do what you say but when I am done I never want you near me again.
speaker: ALAN

text: (Ensemble clock)
speaker: Stage

text: He worked through the night.
speaker: C2

text: The next morning Dorian returned to the schoolroom.
speaker: C5

text: A horrible smell of nitric acid lingered in the room.
speaker: C4

text: But the thing that had been sitting at the table was gone.
speaker: C2

text: Thank you Alan. You have saved my life.
speaker: Dorian

text: I did not do it for you and I do not wish to see your face from this moment on. Stay away from me and all I hold dear. (exits)
speaker: ALAN

text: (Dorian removes the cloth from the portrait and recoils)
speaker: Stage

text: What was that writhing movement?
speaker: C5

text: The cruel mouth twisting.
speaker: All 3

text: What was that deathly echo?
speaker: C5

text: a ghastly voice inside
speaker: All 4

text: What was that red dew glistening?
speaker: C3

text: the canvas sweating blood.
speaker: All 3

text: He ran from the room in horror.
speaker: C4

text: Did something run beside him?
speaker: C2

text: The stench of blood pursued him.
speaker: C5

text: Tortured his fevered brain
speaker: C4

text: Poisoned his wasted soul
speaker: C2

text: He longed for oblivion
speaker: C5

text: Sweet opium called him
speaker: C4

text: His craving carried him
speaker: C2

text: Mindlessly led him
speaker: C5

text: To the beat of his mantra
speaker: C4

text: Cure the soul by means of the senses And the senses by means of the soul
speaker: C2

text: (Chorus surrounds him)
speaker: Stage

text: Cure the soul by means of the senses, and the senses by means of the soul. Cure the soul by means of the senses, and the senses by means of the soul. Cure the soul by means of the senses, and the senses by means of the soul.
